item.content:encoded:
Miklos on Minnie
What were you hoping for? To take a step outside my comfort zone. To meet the love of my life.
First impressions? Confident, and just as confused as I was about how to start off a blind date.
What did you talk about? The optimal time horizon to plan your life ahead – we oscillated between one and 10 years. After that, I’m embarrassed to admit, loads of K-pop.
Most awkward moment? On my way to the loo I stepped on a dog by accident. I felt horrible, but Minnie assured me it was OK.
Good table manners? The food was so intimidatingly tasty it forced the best table manners out of us. Hers were almost too good, I’d say.
Best thing about Minnie? She is from the best part of town (in my opinion) and it shows. She is unabashedly herself.
Would you introduce Minnie to your friends? They love a bottle of wine. She loves a bottle of wine. There is nothing more to say.
Blind date is Saturday’s dating column: every week, two strangers are paired up for dinner and drinks, and then spill the beans to us, answering a set of questions. This runs, with a photograph we take of each dater before the date, in Saturday magazine (in the UK) and online at theguardian.com every Saturday. It’s been running since 2009 – you can read all about how we put it together here. What questions will I be asked? We ask about age, location, occupation, hobbies, interests and the type of person you are looking to meet. If you do not think these questions cover everything you would like to know, tell us what’s on your mind.
Can I choose who I match with? No, it’s a blind date! But we do ask you a bit about your interests, preferences, etc – the more you tell us, the better the match is likely to be.
Can I pick the photograph? No, but don't worry: we'll choose the nicest ones.
What personal details will appear? Your first name, job and age.
How should I answer? Honestly but respectfully. Be mindful of how it will read to your date, and that Blind date reaches a large audience, in print and online.
Will I see the other person’s answers? No. We may edit yours and theirs for a range of reasons, including length, and we may ask you for more details.
Will you find me The One? We’ll try! Marriage! Babies!
Can I do it in my home town? Only if it’s in the UK. Many of our applicants live in London, but we would love to hear from people living elsewhere.
How to apply Email blind.date@theguardian.com
Describe Minnie in three words Talkative. Fuzzy. Edgy.
What do you think Minnie made of you? I think she saw me quite accurately: nerdy, but willing to push boundaries and have some fun.
Did you go on somewhere? We did not.
And ... did you kiss? No kissing was had.
If you could change one thing about the date, what would it be? I wish I had not stepped on that dog – that’s it really.
Marks out of 10? 9.
Would you meet again? By the end of the date, it was clear to both of us that we were missing a romantic spark … That’s life!
Minnie on Miklos
What were you hoping for? A fun evening.
First impressions? Very lovely guy, good vibes. I was a tad late and he was super understanding. He also noted that he often goes by Mickey, which is pretty funny.
What did you talk about? Travel. Studies. Controversial opinions on music concerts. Katseye (sorry, Miklos).
Most awkward moment? Neither of us could figure out the menu.
Good table manners? Yes, very polite.
Best thing about Miklos? He is super different from me. It was nice chatting with someone who has lived such a different life.
Would you introduce Miklos to your friends? Hypothetically yes, but only as a friend.
Related: Blind date: ‘Bizarrely, she suddenly realised she knew my daughter’
Describe Miklos in three words Intelligent, chatty, inquisitive.
What do you think Miklos made of you? That I was easy to talk to.
Did you go on somewhere? Nope, just headed home.
And ... did you kiss? Couple of hugs, not the vibe for a kiss.
If you could change one thing about the date, what would it be? We both said we would have liked to have been in a different part of town by the canal (the restaurant was lovely though).
Marks out of 10? 7.
Would you meet again? Probably not, but no hard feelings.
Miklos and Minnie ate at the Bull and Last, London NW5. Fancy a blind date? Email blind.date@theguardian.com

item.content:encoded:
Go on a blind date. We’ll pick up the tab. Fill out an application at bostonglobe.com/cupid.
NATHAN F.: 24 / food service worker/graduate school student
What makes him a catch: He’s a tall (6 foot 4), well-read, redheaded musician.
Last thing he read: Dubliners by James Joyce
CLAIRE S.: 25 / office manager
When she is happiest: Sitting in the Boston Public Garden with a book
On a desert island, she’d bring: Toothpaste, toothbrush, and floss
8 P.M. PURITAN & CO., CAMBRIDGE
Signs to Come
Nathan I drove up from a wedding the day of the date. I arrived in time to shower and take the train down. I met a friend and we walked to the spot together, at which point I kindly told him to go find something else to do.
Claire I got ready with my roommates.
Nathan My first impression was, Wow, this girl is short! (She is 5 foot 2.) And then, Woah, she’s dressed kind of badass, because she was rocking a black leather jacket.
Claire He’s very tall! He’s handsome too, and has nice hair.
Higher Power
Nathan We talked about our jobs and where we’re hoping to go in our lives. Turns out, we’re both considering becoming social workers. I was genuinely riveted when she told me her horror stories from summer camp. She also told me she doesn’t listen to music on her commute because she likes to use that time to daydream. I thought that was one of the most interesting things I’d ever been told.
Claire I learned that he was taking a break from divinity school, and that he had been researching substance-use disorders through a spiritual lens. My work relates to mental health, so I was immediately interested in learning more. We spoke about what inspired him to study religion in undergrad and talked about the different religions he learned about. Also, he told me he was in a band, and plays the bass.
Nathan We ordered some grilled zucchini and a large crab cake, and a round of oysters. Later, we got the tuna carpaccio.
Claire The carpaccio was the standout. We also had some champagne and then I tried the Northern Lights cocktail, which was also delicious.
Nathan This first date was noticeably more comfortable than others I’ve been on. We began to tease each other more and care less about what exactly was being talked about.
Claire He’s very easy to talk to. On the way out I grabbed his arm, and we ended up holding hands. It was sweet.
Open Minds
Nathan I was excited to continue the date, so while she washed up I chitchatted with the staff to assess our options.
Claire After dinner, Nathan suggested two bars nearby. I was happy to continue the evening, so we headed to one.
Nathan The date ended with me walking her home. We were pretty happy in each other’s company on the walk back, it seemed to me; I went to give her a little spin at the end of the date and she misinterpreted it, fairly, I think, as a handshake. I was hoping we might feel a little chemistry in that moment, but it didn’t really work out — which is OK!
Claire He offered to walk me home, which I thought was nice. We stood at the corner and chatted for a bit longer, and then we hugged and parted ways.
Second Date?
Nathan I think we will! We have begun chitchatting about it.
Claire I would! I don’t see us running out of conversation topics anytime soon.
Grading the Date
Nathan / B+
Claire / A
Go on a blind date. We’ll pick up the tab. Fill out an application at bostonglobe.com/cupid.

item.content:encoded:
Dec on Dave
What were you hoping for?
A sweet-hearted madman who would make me belly laugh.
First impressions?
Looked like a David. A bit nervous and jittery, but considerate, curious and chatty (all the best C-words).
What did you talk about?
People in cars shouting “ginge” at him. Us coming from the West Country (but only I sound like it). How I don’t like Clapham gays – guess where he lives?
Most awkward moment?
I tried on his stethoscope, pretending to listen for a heartbeat from the chicken.
Good table manners?
Sound as a pound.
Best thing about David?
His passion for his profession. Also, how he was so keen to ask, listen and hear.
Would you introduce David to your friends?
Possibly, so they can give him his second Buzzballz ever!
Describe David in three words
Moustached, kind, grounded.
What do you think David made of you?
Probably an absolute loony. No, I wonder if he saw through the tarty humour to my kind, smart, caring self.
Did you go on somewhere?
The kitchen was closing, and he had to work in the morning, saving lives – very inconsiderate.
And … did you kiss?
I gave him a polite peck on the cheek when we hugged bye-bye.
If you could change one thing about the evening, what would it be?
Nothing: it was the perfect balance of sincere connection and nonsense.
Marks out of 10?
A solid 6. He’s a cracking bloke and rocks a floral shirt better than anyone I know. It’s a 6 not a 7 because I don’t like fish or salad; he kindly ordered me both.
Would you meet again?
We swapped numbers. We’re not each other’s “spark”, but had a good evening.
David on Dec
What were you hoping for?
Someone who put me at ease, asked me questions and made me want to text my friends about him in the toilet.
First impressions?
Definitely a main character. Handsome, potty-mouthed, charming and equally clueless about tapas.
What did you talk about?
Dec’s love of swearing. Coming out.
Most awkward moment?
Possibly when I realised I had a child’s blood on my trousers.
Good table manners?
Impeccable.
Best thing about Dec?
He’s very free and at ease in himself, and made me feel I could be too. And his autobiography will be a bestseller.
Would you introduce Dec to your friends?
I would. But I didn’t toilet-text them.
Describe Dec in three words
Curious, beautiful, free.
What do you think Dec made of you?
Hopefully good company! “Doctor” brings a whole set of expectations, but it felt like he was able to see past all that.
Did you go on somewhere?
We didn’t – but we stayed until closing.
And … did you kiss?
A quick peck at the station.
If you could change one thing about the evening, what would it be?
We were side-by-side at the bar, which is weird for a first date. And he got my right side, which is definitely less good.
Marks out of 10?
8.
Would you meet again?
We agreed the chemistry felt more friendly than romantic, but I’d love to stay in touch.
Dec and David ate at Barrafina Drury Lane, London WC2. Fancy a blind date? Email blind.date@theguardian.com
